Repo: /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim/QEMU (a QEMU fork). You are doing a SIMPLIFICATION-angle code-quality review. REPORT ONLY — do not edit any files.

Scope: the STAGED changes (uncommitted, at a detached HEAD). Get them with `git diff --cached`. The changes are commit 1 of a refactor: the "hotloops" tool. Files:
- contrib/plugins/hotloops.c (NEW, ~191 lines) — a TCG plugin that detects loops via backward TB transitions
- contrib/plugins/meson.build (modified, +3)
- scripts/hotloops.sh (NEW, ~566 lines) — bash wrapper: rv32/rv64 autodetect, baremetal qemu-system runner, RVV-only filter, LLM/table report, objdump+addr2line symbol/source resolution
- docs/hotloops.md (NEW)
Read the new files in full.

Your angle — SIMPLIFICATION: flag unnecessary complexity the code adds.
- Redundant or derivable state (variables that can be computed/removed).
- Copy-paste with slight variation (esp. in the 566-line bash script — repeated awk/objdump/addr2line blocks, repeated arg-parse branches, near-duplicate report-emit code for table vs LLM mode).
- Deep nesting that flattens with early-return/guard clauses.
- Dead code, unused vars, unreachable branches.
- Overly clever one-liners that a clearer form replaces.
Name the simpler form that does the same job. For each finding: file, line(s), one-line summary, concrete cost, and the simpler form. Behavior-preserving fixes only. If a section is already clean, say so. Be concise; prioritize the highest-value simplifications.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).

- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

contrib/plugins/hotloops.c  | 191 +++++++++++++++
 contrib/plugins/meson.build |   3 +-
 docs/hotloops.md            | 267 +++++++++++++++++++++
 scripts/hotloops.sh         | 566 ++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 4 files changed, 1026 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Hot inner-loop detector wrapper (system-mode, baremetal RISC-V).
3	#
4	# Runs a baremetal ELF under qemu-system-<arch> with the hotloops plugin
5	# and prints a sorted table of detected backward branches:
6	#
7	#   iters | start_pc -> end_pc | function:offset
8	#
9	# Usage:
10	#   scripts/hotloops.sh [opts] <elf>
11	#
12	# Options:
13	#   --arch <riscv32|riscv64|auto>   Target arch (default: auto)
14	#   --qemu <path>                   Override qemu-system binary
15	#   --plugin <path>                 Override plugin .so
16	#   --machine <name>                -M <name> (default andes_ae350)
17	#   --cpu <spec>                    -cpu <spec>
18	#                                   (default andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024)
19	#   --qemu-config <file>            -readconfig <file> (e.g. AE350 device cfg)
20	#   --cwd <dir>                     chdir before launching QEMU so semihosting
21	#                                   opens (fread of bin/*.bin) resolve
22	#   --qemu-arg <arg>                Append an extra arg to the QEMU command
23	#                                   (repeatable)
24	#   --limit <N>                     Top-N loops to print (default 50)
25	#   --min-iters <N>                 Drop loops with fewer than N iters (default 1)
26	#   --objdump <path>                Override objdump (resolves symbols)
27	#   --addr2line <path>              Override addr2line (resolves source lines)
28	#   --no-source                     Disable source file:line resolution
29	#   --raw                           Print raw plugin output, no formatting
30	#   --optimize-rvv                  Only report loops with at least one RVV
31	#                                   instruction (default: on)
32	#   --no-optimize-rvv               Disable the RVV-only filter
33	#   --llm                           Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM
34	#                                   consumption: TL;DR + per-loop fact-sheets
35	#                                   with stable IDs, source snippets, RVV
36	#                                   instruction listings, nesting, and direct
37	#                                   callees (default: on).
38	#   --no-llm                        Emit the plain human-readable table.
39	#   -h | --help                     Show help
40	
41	set -euo pipefail
42	
43	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
44	QEMU_ROOT="$(cd -- "${SCRIPT_DIR}/.." && pwd)"
45	
46	ARCH="auto"
47	QEMU=""
48	PLUGIN=""
49	LIMIT=50
50	MIN_ITERS=1
51	OBJDUMP=""
52	ADDR2LINE=""
53	NO_SOURCE=0
54	RAW=0
55	OPTIMIZE_RVV=1
56	LLM=1
57	MACHINE="andes_ae350"
58	CPU="andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024"
59	QEMU_CONFIG=""
60	QEMU_CWD=""
61	EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS=()
62	
63	usage() { sed -n '2,39p' "$0"; exit 0; }
64	
65	# --- arg parsing ---
66	ELF=""
67	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
68	    case "$1" in
69	        --arch)        ARCH="$2"; shift 2 ;;
70	        --qemu)        QEMU="$2"; shift 2 ;;
71	        --plugin)      PLUGIN="$2"; shift 2 ;;
72	        --machine)     MACHINE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
73	        --cpu)         CPU="$2"; shift 2 ;;
74	        --qemu-config) QEMU_CONFIG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
75	        --cwd)         QEMU_CWD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
76	        --qemu-arg)    EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS+=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
77	        --limit)       LIMIT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
78	        --min-iters)   MIN_ITERS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
79	        --objdump)     OBJDUMP="$2"; shift 2 ;;
80	        --addr2line)   ADDR2LINE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
81	        --no-source)   NO_SOURCE=1; shift ;;
82	        --raw)         RAW=1; shift ;;
83	        --optimize-rvv)    OPTIMIZE_RVV=1; shift ;;
84	        --no-optimize-rvv) OPTIMIZE_RVV=0; shift ;;
85	        --llm)             LLM=1; shift ;;
86	        --no-llm)          LLM=0; shift ;;
87	        -h|--help)     usage ;;
88	        -*) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
89	        *)
90	            if [[ -z "$ELF" ]]; then
91	                ELF="$1"; shift
92	            else
93	                echo "error: unexpected positional arg: $1" >&2; exit 2
94	            fi ;;
95	    esac
96	done
97	
98	[[ -n "$ELF" ]] || { echo "error: ELF path required" >&2; exit 2; }
99	[[ -f "$ELF" ]] || { echo "error: not found: $ELF" >&2; exit 2; }
100	
101	# --- arch detection ---
102	if [[ "$ARCH" == "auto" ]]; then
103	    file_out="$(file -L -- "$ELF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
104	    case "$file_out" in
105	        *"ELF 64-bit"*"RISC-V"*)  ARCH=riscv64 ;;
106	        *"ELF 32-bit"*"RISC-V"*)  ARCH=riscv32 ;;
107	        *) echo "error: cannot auto-detect arch (not RISC-V?), pass --arch" >&2; exit 2 ;;
108	    esac
109	fi
110	
111	# --- locate qemu + plugin ---
112	if [[ -z "$QEMU" ]]; then
113	    QEMU="${QEMU_ROOT}/build/qemu-system-${ARCH}"
114	fi
115	[[ -x "$QEMU" ]] || { echo "error: qemu not found/executable: $QEMU" >&2; exit 2; }
116	
117	if [[ -z "$PLUGIN" ]]; then
118	    PLUGIN="${QEMU_ROOT}/build/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so"
119	fi
120	[[ -f "$PLUGIN" ]] || { echo "error: plugin not built: $PLUGIN" >&2; exit 2; }
121	
122	# --- run ---
123	LOG="$(mktemp -t hotloops.XXXXXX.log)"
124	trap 'rm -f "$LOG"' EXIT
125	
126	QEMU_CMD=("$QEMU"
127	          -plugin "${PLUGIN},limit=${LIMIT},min_iters=${MIN_ITERS}"
128	          -d plugin -D "$LOG"
129	          -M "$MACHINE"
130	          -cpu "$CPU"
131	          -nographic -semihosting
132	          -bios "$ELF")
133	[[ -n "$QEMU_CONFIG" ]] && QEMU_CMD+=(-readconfig "$QEMU_CONFIG")
134	[[ ${#EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS[@]} -gt 0 ]] && QEMU_CMD+=("${EXTRA_QEMU_ARGS[@]}")
135	if [[ -n "$QEMU_CWD" ]]; then
136	    ( cd "$QEMU_CWD" && "${QEMU_CMD[@]}" ) >/dev/null
137	else
138	    "${QEMU_CMD[@]}" >/dev/null
139	fi
140	
141	if [[ "$RAW" -eq 1 ]]; then
142	    cat "$LOG"
143	    exit 0
144	fi
145	
146	# --- symbol table from objdump (best effort) ---
147	if [[ -z "$OBJDUMP" ]]; then
148	    for cand in llvm-objdump riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump \
149	                riscv32-unknown-elf-objdump objdump; do
150	        if command -v "$cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
151	            OBJDUMP="$cand"
152	            break
153	        fi
154	    done
155	fi
156	
157	SYMS="$(mktemp -t hotloops_syms.XXXXXX)"
158	LINES="$(mktemp -t hotloops_lines.XXXXXX)"
159	DISASM="$(mktemp -t hotloops_disasm.XXXXXX)"
160	trap 'rm -f "$LOG" "$SYMS" "$LINES" "$DISASM"' EXIT
161	if [[ -n "$OBJDUMP" ]]; then
162	    # Capture FUNC symbols: addr size type name
163	    "$OBJDUMP" -t "$ELF" 2>/dev/null \
164	        | awk 'tolower($0) ~ /[ \t]f[ \t]/ && NF>=5 {
165	                  addr=strtonum("0x" $1);
166	                  size=strtonum("0x" $(NF-1));
167	                  name=$NF;
168	                  if (size>0) print addr, size, name;
169	              }' \
170	        | sort -n -k1,1 > "$SYMS" || true
171	
172	    # Capture disassembly: each output line is "<hex-pc> <mnemonic> <operands>".
173	    # Works for both GNU binutils objdump and llvm-objdump. Used by the RVV
174	    # filter (mnemonic) and --llm mode (operands, callee names).
175	    if [[ "$OPTIMIZE_RVV" -eq 1 || "$LLM" -eq 1 ]]; then
176	        "$OBJDUMP" -d --no-show-raw-insn "$ELF" 2>/dev/null \
177	            | awk '
178	                /^[ \t]*[0-9a-fA-F]+:[ \t]+[^ \t]+/ {
179	                    line = $0;
180	                    sub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line);
181	                    sub(/[ \t]+$/, "", line);
182	                    sub(/:[ \t]+/, " ", line);
183	                    print line;
184	                }' > "$DISASM" || true
185	    fi
186	fi
187	
188	# --- locate addr2line for source line resolution (DWARF) ---
189	if [[ "$NO_SOURCE" -eq 0 && -z "$ADDR2LINE" ]]; then
190	    for cand in llvm-addr2line addr2line \
191	                riscv64-unknown-elf-addr2line riscv32-unknown-elf-addr2line \
192	                riscv64-linux-gnu-addr2line; do
193	        if command -v "$cand" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
194	            ADDR2LINE="$cand"
195	            break
196	        fi
197	    done
198	fi
199	
200	# Pre-collect all PCs from the log and batch-resolve to file:line.
201	# LINES file format: <hex-pc> <file:line>
202	if [[ "$NO_SOURCE" -eq 0 && -n "$ADDR2LINE" ]]; then
203	    pcs="$(awk -F',' '/^0x/ {gsub(/[ \t]/,"",$1); gsub(/[ \t]/,"",$2); print $1; print $2}' "$LOG" | sort -u)"
204	    if [[ -n "$pcs" ]]; then
205	        # addr2line: -e <elf> reads addrs on stdin, prints file:line.
206	        # We keep full paths here (no -s) so --llm mode can locate the
207	        # source file for code snippets; table mode basenames in Python.
208	        out="$(printf '%s\n' $pcs | "$ADDR2LINE" -e "$ELF" 2>/dev/null || true)"
209	        paste <(printf '%s\n' $pcs) <(printf '%s\n' "$out") > "$LINES" || true
210	    fi
211	fi
212	
213	# --- format ---
214	python3 - "$LOG" "$SYMS" "$LINES" "$DISASM" "$LIMIT" "$MIN_ITERS" \
215	        "$OPTIMIZE_RVV" "$LLM" "$ELF" <<'PY'
216	import sys, os, re, bisect
217	
218	log_path     = sys.argv[1]
219	syms_path    = sys.argv[2]
220	lines_path   = sys.argv[3]
221	disasm_path  = sys.argv[4]
222	limit        = int(sys.argv[5])
223	min_iters    = int(sys.argv[6])
224	optimize_rvv = int(sys.argv[7]) == 1
225	llm_mode     = int(sys.argv[8]) == 1
226	elf_path     = sys.argv[9]
227	
228	# --- symbols (FUNC syms): list of (addr, size, name) sorted by addr ---
229	syms = []
230	try:
231	    with open(syms_path) as f:
232	        for line in f:
233	            parts = line.split()
234	            if len(parts) >= 3:
235	                syms.append((int(parts[0]), int(parts[1]),
236	                             " ".join(parts[2:])))
237	except FileNotFoundError:
238	    pass
239	
240	def resolve(pc):
241	    for addr, size, name in syms:
242	        if addr <= pc < addr + size:
243	            return f"{name}+0x{pc-addr:x}"
244	    return "?"
245	
246	def fn_of(pc):
247	    for addr, size, name in syms:
248	        if addr <= pc < addr + size:
249	            return name
250	    return None
251	
252	# --- source map: pc -> "path:line" (full path; basename in Python for table) ---
253	src_map = {}
254	try:
255	    with open(lines_path) as f:
256	        for line in f:
257	            parts = line.rstrip("\n").split("\t", 1)
258	            if len(parts) == 2:
259	                pc_str, src = parts
260	                src = src.strip()
261	                if src and not src.startswith("??"):
262	                    try:
263	                        src_map[int(pc_str, 16)] = src
264	                    except ValueError:
265	                        pass
266	except FileNotFoundError:
267	    pass
268	
269	def src_full(pc):
270	    return src_map.get(pc, "")
271	
272	def src_basename(s):
273	    """Basename the path part of a 'path:line[ (extra)]' string."""
274	    if not s:
275	        return ""
276	    head, sep, tail = s.partition(" ")
277	    return os.path.basename(head) + (sep + tail if sep else "")
278	
279	def src_short(pc):
280	    return src_basename(src_full(pc))
281	
282	# --- disassembly: pc -> (mnemonic, operands) ---
283	disasm = {}
284	try:
285	    with open(disasm_path) as f:
286	        for line in f:
287	            line = line.rstrip("\n")
288	            parts = line.split(None, 2)
289	            if len(parts) < 2:
290	                continue
291	            try:
292	                pc = int(parts[0], 16)
293	            except ValueError:
294	                continue
295	            mnemonic = parts[1]
296	            operands = parts[2] if len(parts) >= 3 else ""
297	            disasm[pc] = (mnemonic, operands)
298	except FileNotFoundError:
299	    pass
300	
301	disasm_pcs = sorted(disasm.keys())
302	
303	def is_rvv_mnemonic(mn):
304	    mn = mn.lower()
305	    return mn.startswith("v") and len(mn) > 1 and mn[1].isalpha()
306	
307	rvv_pcs = sorted(pc for pc, (mn, _) in disasm.items() if is_rvv_mnemonic(mn))
308	
309	def has_rvv_in_range(s, e):
310	    if not rvv_pcs or s > e:
311	        return False
312	    i = bisect.bisect_left(rvv_pcs, s)
313	    return i < len(rvv_pcs) and rvv_pcs[i] <= e
314	
315	def rvv_insns_in_range(s, e):
316	    out = []
317	    if not rvv_pcs or s > e:
318	        return out
319	    i = bisect.bisect_left(rvv_pcs, s)
320	    while i < len(rvv_pcs) and rvv_pcs[i] <= e:
321	        pc = rvv_pcs[i]
322	        mn, ops = disasm[pc]
323	        out.append((pc, mn, ops))
324	        i += 1
325	    return out
326	
327	CALL_MN = {"jal", "jalr", "c.jal", "c.jalr"}
328	CALLEE_RE = re.compile(r"<([^>]+)>")
329	
330	def calls_in_range(s, e):
331	    out = []
332	    if not disasm_pcs or s > e:
333	        return out
334	    i = bisect.bisect_left(disasm_pcs, s)
335	    while i < len(disasm_pcs) and disasm_pcs[i] <= e:
336	        pc = disasm_pcs[i]
337	        mn, ops = disasm[pc]
338	        if mn in CALL_MN:
339	            m = CALLEE_RE.search(ops)
340	            target = m.group(1) if m else "(indirect)"
341	            out.append((pc, mn, target))
342	        i += 1
343	    return out
344	
345	def parse_file_line(s):
346	    """'path:42' or 'path:42 (discriminator 1)' -> (path, 42)."""
347	    if not s or s.startswith("??"):
348	        return None, None
349	    m = re.match(r"^(.+?):(\d+)(?::\d+)?(?:\s|$)", s)
350	    if not m:
351	        return None, None
352	    return m.group(1), int(m.group(2))
353	
354	def read_source_line(path, lineno):

411	    best_size = None

415	        if cand.start <= loop.start and loop.end <= cand.end:
416	            if cand.start == loop.start and cand.end == loop.end:
417	                continue  # identical range, ambiguous - skip
418	            sz = cand.end - cand.start
419	            if best is None or sz < best_size:
420	                best = cand
421	                best_size = sz

1	# hotloops - hot inner-loop detector
2	
3	Detects the hottest loops in a baremetal RISC-V ELF by observing backward
4	translation-block transitions in `qemu-system-<arch>`. For each detected
5	loop you get the loop header PC, the backward-branch PC, and the iteration
6	count. With DWARF, you also get the source `file:line`. With objdump
7	present, you get RVV-only filtering and per-loop disassembly context.
8	
9	Two parts ship together:
10	
11	- `contrib/plugins/hotloops.c` - QEMU TCG plugin that records edges.
12	- `scripts/hotloops.sh` - wrapper that runs the plugin and formats output.
13	
14	## Usage
15	
16	```
17	scripts/hotloops.sh [options] <elf>
18	```
19	
20	The wrapper launches `qemu-system-<arch>` with `-bios <elf>` on a baremetal
21	machine (default `andes_ae350`) and a vector-capable CPU (default
22	`andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024`). Override per the options below
23	for other targets.
24	
25	### Options
26	
27	| Flag                | Default            | Description                                                    |
28	|---------------------|--------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
29	| `--arch <a>`        | auto               | Target arch: `riscv32`, `riscv64`, or `auto` (from `file`).    |
30	| `--qemu <path>`     | auto               | Override the `qemu-system-<arch>` binary.                      |
31	| `--plugin <path>`   | auto               | Override the plugin `.so`.                                     |
32	| `--machine <name>`  | `andes_ae350`      | `-M <name>` passed to QEMU.                                    |
33	| `--cpu <spec>`      | `andes-ax45mpv,...`| `-cpu <spec>` passed to QEMU. Default enables RVV 1.0 vlen=1024.|
34	| `--qemu-config <f>` | -                  | `-readconfig <file>` (e.g. AE350 device cfg).                  |
35	| `--cwd <dir>`       | -                  | `chdir` before launching QEMU (so semihosting `fread` of `bin/*.bin` resolves). |
36	| `--qemu-arg <arg>`  | -                  | Extra arg appended to the QEMU command. Repeatable.            |
37	| `--limit <N>`       | 50                 | Print at most N loops.                                         |
38	| `--min-iters <N>`   | 1                  | Drop loops with fewer than N iterations (hot-loop threshold).  |
39	| `--objdump <path>`  | auto               | Override objdump (for `function+offset` and disassembly).      |
40	| `--addr2line <path>`| auto               | Override addr2line (for source-line resolution).               |
41	| `--no-source`       | off                | Skip source resolution even if DWARF is present.               |
42	| `--raw`             | off                | Print raw plugin output (CSV-ish), no formatting.              |
43	| `--optimize-rvv`    | on                 | Only report loops that contain at least one RVV instruction.   |
44	| `--no-optimize-rvv` | off                | Disable the RVV-only filter; report all loops.                 |
45	| `--llm`             | on                 | Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption (see below).  |
46	| `--no-llm`          | off                | Emit the plain human-readable table instead of the LLM report. |
47	
48	### Build prerequisites
49	
50	The plugin lives in `contrib/plugins/`. Build once:
51	
52	```
53	ninja -C build contrib-plugins
54	```
55	
56	It is incremental on subsequent edits to `hotloops.c`. The QEMU binaries
57	themselves (`qemu-system-riscv64`, `qemu-system-riscv32`) do **not** need
58	to be rebuilt.
59	
60	## How it detects a loop
61	
62	For every translated block, the plugin remembers the PC of its last
63	instruction. When the next-executed block starts at a PC `<=` that
64	remembered PC, the transition is a backward edge - i.e. a loop iteration.
65	The pair `(header_pc, tail_pc)` is the key; the count is the number of
66	iterations.
67	
68	This catches every loop a real backward branch closes (for/while/do-while,
69	goto, manually unrolled tails, etc.) without needing to model branch
70	semantics.
71	
72	Caveat: each iteration counted is one *taken* backward branch. A loop
73	that runs N times has N-1 taken backward branches plus one fall-through
74	on exit, so the reported count is N-1 per call to the enclosing function.
75	
76	## Output modes
77	
78	Three output modes, in order of layered post-processing:
79	
80	1. `--llm` (default on) - Markdown report tuned for LLM consumption.
81	2. `--no-llm` - plain human-readable table.
82	3. `--raw` - unformatted plugin output (overrides the above).
83	
84	### LLM report (default)
85	
86	The wrapper emits a single Markdown document structured so an LLM (or a
87	reader skimming top-down) can answer "what is the hottest loop?" from the
88	first paragraph, then drill down via stable IDs.
89	
90	Layout:
91	
92	- Header block: `target`, `total_iters`, `reported_loops`, `min_iters`,
93	  `rvv_filter`.
94	- `## TL;DR` paragraph naming the hottest loop, its function and source
95	  line, percentage of total iterations, RVV vs scalar (with the top-K
96	  unique vector mnemonics seen), and nesting status.
97	- One `### L<N>` fact-sheet per reported loop (sorted by iters desc):
98	  - `iters` and `pc_range` (`0xstart .. 0xend  (size: N B)`).
99	  - `function` (`fn+0xoff -> fn+0xoff`).
100	  - `source` (`file:line` or `file:line -> file:line` if the header and
101	    tail map to different lines).
102	  - `code` - inline best-effort source snippet read from the path stored
103	    in DWARF.
104	  - `rvv` summary plus `rvv_insns:` listing (capped at 8) with each
105	    `0xpc  mnemonic operands`.
106	  - `parent` / `children` - stable IDs of containing / contained loops.
107	    Inferred from PC-range containment, so this captures only
108	    same-function nesting.
109	  - `calls` - direct callees inside the loop body (`jal`/`jalr` with a
110	    statically known target via the `<name>` annotation). Indirect calls
111	    show as `(indirect)`.
112	
113	The TL;DR is templated from the same data fields the per-loop blocks use;
114	no LLM call is made by the script itself.
115	
116	Limitations:
117	
118	- Same-function nesting only. A caller's hot loop that calls a callee
119	  containing its own hot loop will show as two unrelated loops; follow
120	  `calls:` to bridge.
121	- `code:` snippets require the source file to be reachable at the
122	  absolute path stored in DWARF. Cross-compiled or relocated builds may
123	  fall back to just `file:line`.
124	- The RVV filter is mnemonic-based: any insn whose mnemonic begins with
125	  `v<alpha>` (e.g. `vsetvli`, `vle32.v`, `vadd.vv`, `vmul.vv`). Standard
126	  scalar RISC-V has no such mnemonic, so this is exact in practice.
127	
128	### Table mode (`--no-llm`)
129	
130	Header line, then a fixed-width table sorted by `iters` descending:
131	
132	```
133	# hot loops (iters >= <threshold>[, RVV-only]), sorted desc, top <K>
134	iters | start_pc           -> end_pc             | location              | source
135	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
136	<n>   | 0x<16-hex>         -> 0x<16-hex>         | <fn>+0x<o> -> <fn>+0x<o> | file:line -> file:line
137	...
138	```
139	
140	Columns:
141	
142	- `iters`     - taken backward-branch count (sorted desc).
143	- `start_pc`  - PC of the loop header (the branch target).
144	- `end_pc`    - PC of the backward branch (the loop tail).
145	- `location`  - `function+offset -> function+offset` from the ELF symbol
146	                table. Shows `?` if the address is not inside any sized
147	                FUNC symbol.
148	- `source`    - `file:line -> file:line` from DWARF (basenamed).
149	                Collapsed to a single `file:line` when both ends map to
150	                the same source line. Only present when the ELF has debug
151	                info and `--no-source` is not set.
152	
153	### Raw mode (`--raw`)
154	
155	Bypasses both the LLM report and the table, printing the unformatted
156	plugin output:
157	
158	```
159	hotloops: <distinct> distinct backward edges, <hot> hot (>= <thr> iters), sorted by iterations desc
160	start_pc, end_pc, iterations
161	0x..., 0x..., <n>
162	...
163	```
164	
165	Stable across releases - useful for piping into another tool.
166	
167	## Example
168	
169	A doubly-nested loop with an RVV inner body:
170	
171	```c
172	/* hotloops_demo.c - baremetal entry */
173	#include <stdint.h>
174	
175	__attribute__((noinline))
176	static int dot_rvv(const int *a, const int *b, int n) {
177	    int s = 0;
178	    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
179	    return s;
180	}
181	
182	void main(void) {
183	    static int a[64], b[64];
184	    for (int i = 0; i < 64; i++) { a[i] = i; b[i] = 64 - i; }
185	    long total = 0;
186	    for (int outer = 0; outer < 500; outer++)
187	        total += dot_rvv(a, b, 64);                  /* 64 * 500 inner iters */
188	    (void)total;
189	}
190	```
191	
192	Build for AE350 with the Andes RISC-V toolchain (or any baremetal
193	RVV-capable toolchain), then run:
194	
195	```
196	$ scripts/hotloops.sh --min-iters 100 --limit 5 build/hotloops_demo.elf
197	```
198	
199	LLM-mode output (the default) looks like:
200	
201	```markdown
202	# Hotloops Report
203	target:           hotloops_demo.elf
204	total_iters:      32000
205	reported_loops:   1
206	min_iters:        100
207	rvv_filter:       on
208	
209	## TL;DR
210	Hottest loop is L1 in `dot_rvv` (hotloops_demo.c:6), 31500 iters = 98.4% of
211	total. Body is RVV (vsetvli, vle32.v, vmul.vv, +1 more). It is top-level
212	(no parent loop), and contains no inner loop.
213	
214	## Loops
215	
216	### L1 [hottest]  (98.4% of total)
217	iters:        31500
218	pc_range:     0x80000200 .. 0x80000218  (size: 24 B)
219	function:     dot_rvv+0x10 -> dot_rvv+0x28
220	source:       hotloops_demo.c:6
221	code:         for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) s += a[i] * b[i];   /* line 6, vectorized */
222	rvv:          yes (4 insns)
223	rvv_insns:
224	  - 0x80000200  vsetvli    t0,a2,e32,m1,ta,ma
225	  - 0x80000208  vle32.v    v1,(a0)
226	  - 0x8000020c  vmul.vv    v2,v1,v3
227	  - 0x80000210  vadd.vv    v4,v4,v2
228	parent:       -
229	children:     []
230	calls:        []
231	```
232	
233	Reading the report:
234	
235	- The TL;DR alone identifies the hot path: `dot_rvv` line 6, 98.4% of all
236	  taken backward branches, RVV-vectorized.
237	- `iters = 31500` is close to the expected `64 * 500 = 32000`; the missing
238	  500 are the per-call exits (last iter of `dot_rvv` falls through instead
239	  of branching back).
240	- The 500-iter outer loop in `main` was filtered out by `--min-iters 100`.
241	  It would also have been filtered by the default RVV-only filter since
242	  `main`'s body is scalar (drop with `--no-optimize-rvv` to see scalar
243	  loops too).
244	
245	For piping into a different tool, use `--raw`:
246	
247	```
248	$ scripts/hotloops.sh --raw build/hotloops_demo.elf | head
249	hotloops: 1 distinct backward edges, 1 hot (>= 1 iters), sorted by iterations desc
250	start_pc, end_pc, iterations
251	0x0000000080000200, 0x0000000080000218, 31500
252	```
253	
254	## Tips
255	
256	- Strip rarely-interesting startup loops by raising `--min-iters` to a
257	  value above your background noise floor (e.g. `--min-iters 1000` for a
258	  workload that runs your hot path millions of times).
259	- For a very short workload, lower `--min-iters` and raise `--limit`
260	  to see the full distribution.
261	- Default settings filter to RVV-containing loops only; pair with
262	  `--no-optimize-rvv` if you also want to see the scalar hot spots
263	  (e.g. an outer driver loop wrapping a vectorized kernel).
264	- For LLM consumption, pipe the default output straight into your prompt
265	  - the TL;DR is in the first ~10 lines and the per-loop blocks are
266	  cross-referenceable by their `L<N>` IDs.
267	- `--raw` is the stable interface for downstream tooling.
